title: Binary and Source Compatibility on Kotlin/JVM Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies binary and source compatibility on kotlin/jvm?
options: Combine API and bytecode comparison with old-compiled consumer execution, source rebuilds, and behavioral contract tests.
questions.answer: Combine API and bytecode comparison with old-compiled consumer execution, source rebuilds, and behavioral contract tests.
questions.explanation: The correct response preserves authority, compatibility, exact artifact evidence, adverse-path behavior, and operational ownership.

questions.prompt: Passing a binary API validator proves that the SDK behavior and Android resources remain compatible.
questions.explanation: Updating an API dump after an accidental break only blesses the new surface; it does not make existing compiled clients compatible.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest direct binary compatibility test?
questions.answer: Run a consumer compiled against the old library using the candidate replacement without recompiling the consumer.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the contract or mechanism that remains valid beyond one implementation demonstration.
